name: Colorado

notes: Groceries: exempt from the 2.9% state tax; many home-rule and statutory cities and some counties tax food.
Barber and beauty services, laundry and dry cleaning, and auto repair labor: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).
Motor fuel is exempt from the general sales tax (per-gallon excise instead).
Tobacco is assumed taxed at the general rate (excise taxes left out); not verified state by state.
gaps: Local rates missing for all of Colorado: counties, cities and towns (statutory and home-rule), RTD, and special districts (cultural facilities, mass transit, regional transportation, PIDs). Only the 2.9% state rate is filled in, so Colorado totals here are understated.

Why: CDOR publishes DR 1002 (Colorado Sales/Use Tax Rates) on tax.colorado.gov only as an interactive Looker Studio report, and that site refuses scripted downloads. Its address lookup tool (colorado.ttr.services) has a published pause on bulk lookups. The PDF copy in the State Publications Library could not be downloaded from this workspace. None of these was worked around.

To complete: download the DR 1002 PDF (January 2026: https://spl.cde.state.co.us/artemis/revserials/rev914internet/rev914202601internet.pdf, or the July 2026 edition) by hand into national/raw/rates/CO/, then parse its county and city tables in rates/co.py.
Home-rule cities (Denver, Aurora, Colorado Springs and others) collect their own tax and may tax differently from the state.
